clue.text: Vehicle that's found in a nuclear power plant?

parts.words: Vehicle that's found in a nuclear power plant?
parts.note: surface reading: some kind of transport used inside a reactor building
setter's reading: a reactor core holds fuel elements that run at high temperature, and a phrase for such an element also names a souped-up car

explanation.walkthrough: A hot rod is a modified car tuned for speed; read literally it is a heated rod, the kind of thing at the core of a nuclear reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car rebuilt for extra speed, which is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Healthy-sounding old lady with really empty prayer

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take the word for healthy as it is heard, not as it is spelt

parts.note: hale means healthy, and it is said the same as hail
one's old lady is one's mother, MA

indicators.note: an empty word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of really

explanation.surface: An elderly woman with a robust voice offers up a prayer that is utterly hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is the Catholic prayer to the Virgin, also called the Ave Maria.

clue.text: Pest upset hosts with noise from guitar

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top
something that hosts another takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a gnat is an annoying insect, a pest
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: An irritating person, in a bad mood, puts up guests while making a racket on the guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the sharp ringing sound of a plucked string, typical of a guitar.

clue.text: Unlimited alcoholic beverage — rum

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a toddy is a hot drink of spirits, sugar and water

explanation.surface: A bottomless supply of strong drink, specifically rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink being named, but it is the definition in its sense of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old-fashioned British word for strange or peculiar, the same meaning as odd.

clue.text: Film family with head of Kuwait wearing medal

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: to be wearing something is to have it around you, so the letter sits inside the medal word

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or award

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Kuwait

explanation.surface: A cinema story about a Kuwaiti ruling family whose head wears a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The K goes just inside the gong, after its G; gong is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: King Kong is the 1933 monster movie about a giant ape, remade several times since.

clue.text: Trendy drink I had is tasteless

parts.note: in means fashionable
to sip is to drink a little
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A complaint that the fashionable drink I ordered had no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour, which is the literal sense of tasteless.

clue.text: Leader of Genesis finally performing cover for musical festival

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the first letter of Genesis
last means finally, at the end
a performer is on stage
to bury something is to cover it up

explanation.surface: The Genesis frontman at last takes the stage at a big music festival, perhaps doing a cover version.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is the rock band, which makes 'Leader' look like its singer; here it only takes the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glastonbury is the huge annual music festival held on a farm in Somerset, England.

clue.text: New advert for bank loan of sorts

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bank runs a fresh advertisement for a particular type of loan.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft lets a customer spend more than the account holds, so it works as a short-term loan from the bank.

clue.text: Almost get car delivery in June, perhaps

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gets the new car they ordered delivered in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' sounds like the car arriving, but it is a baby delivered: one born in late May or June is a Gemini.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby born in June is likely to have the star sign Gemini, which runs from late May to late June.

clue.text: Scoundrel seen in river for some time

indicators.note: to be seen in a place is to be inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the English–Welsh border
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue has been spotted down by the river for quite a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade is a period of ten years, so it is some time.

clue.text: With tablet, prepare unique identifier

parts.note: the iPad is Apple's tablet computer
to dress food or a wound is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Instructions to get ready using a tablet computer and some special code.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free IPAD stands in for the brand; 'With' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An IP address is the number that uniquely identifies a device on a network.

clue.text: Lincoln, say, gets a motorway directly from port?

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was known as Abe
taken as written
M is the prefix for British motorways, as in M1

explanation.surface: A man called Lincoln takes a motorway straight from the harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour, but it is the left side of a ship; abeam means at right angles to the ship's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam describes a bearing level with the middle of a ship, straight out from its side, such as its port side.

clue.text: Legendary vehicle — British sports car — without a fresh practice

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the car's letters go around the next small word

parts.note: MG is a British sports car marque
taken as written

indicators.note: a fresh version is newly made, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mythical vehicle is pictured as a British sports car lacking a new training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it is the old sense of outside: M and G sit either side of A.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic carpet that flies its rider through the air is the vehicle of Arabian Nights legend.

clue.text: Pelicans go flying, circling unknown birds that can't fly?

indicators.note: circling something means going around it, so these letters surround the next piece
the words go flying, scattered about and landing in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Pelicans take off and circle some mysterious birds that are grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: these birds are clay discs that do not fly on their own but are flung for shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay pigeons are discs thrown into the air as targets in trap shooting, named after birds but unable to fly.

clue.text: Academic wear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
second meaning: to put on clothing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of scholarly clothing; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A university lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge is called a don, and to don a coat is to put it on.

clue.text: Riot's anger engulfing a politician

indicators.note: to engulf something is to swallow it up, so these letters go around the others

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The fury of rioters sweeps up a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of wild, violent behaviour, which is what a riot is.

clue.text: Thomas, say, tailed horse-like figure

indicators.note: a tailed word has had its tail cut off, losing its final letter

parts.note: Thomas Mann was the German novelist; 'say' marks him as one example of the surname
equine means relating to or resembling horses

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas has a figure like a horse with a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' suggests a horse's tail but means docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a dummy model of the human body used to display clothes, a figure.

clue.text: Refusal to negotiate about Northern Ireland

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to deal is to do business or negotiate
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A refusal to hold talks over the Northern Irish question.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Refusal to negotiate' one phrase; the definition is only 'Refusal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal of a request or a rejection of a claim.

clue.text: I'd return to shift trespasser

indicators.note: to shift is to move about, so the letters change places

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone plans to come back to move a person off their land.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters a place without permission, as a trespasser does.

clue.text: Oil producers claim poles without being asked

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the larger word takes the others in

parts.note: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Oil-producing nations lay claim to the polar regions unprompted.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on spec means doing it speculatively, without being commissioned or asked.

clue.text: Embarrassed, guilty party covers lips

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps around it, so these letters sit outside

parts.note: a con is a convict, someone found guilty
a lip is the rim of a vessel

explanation.surface: A culprit, red-faced, hides their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lips' suggests a mouth, but it means the edges of cups or jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, turning crimson, so the colour stands for the feeling.

clue.text: Pig has good time in town

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the place name

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A pig enjoys itself on a trip into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' looks like the animal, but it is the insult for someone who overeats.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a greedy eater a pig is calling them a glutton.

clue.text: Gareth with award picked up for summerhouse

parts.note: Gaz is a common British nickname for Gareth

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word reads upward, from its end back to its start

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A man named Gareth collects a prize for his garden building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts one toward a homophone, but in a down clue it lifts the award so it reads upward. The OBE is an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open-sided garden building, a kind of summerhouse.

clue.text: Grounds for university to break up scam

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart so its letters can be reassembled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Reasons a university might give for shutting down a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'up' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university, its grounds.

clue.text: Had a meal with friend, skipping starter

indicators.note: skipping the starter means leaving out the first course, so the opening letter is missed

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Dined with a pal but passed on the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to have a meal, so the past tense matches had a meal.

clue.text: Crying and complaining, put up with large animal

parts.note: grizzly is British for whining or crying fretfully, as a child does
to bear is to tolerate

explanation.surface: Someone whining and grumbling while tolerating a big beast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a grizzly child is one who whines and cries.
explanation.definitionFit: The grizzly is a huge North American brown bear, a large animal.

clue.text: European movie villain's short skirt

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Darth Vader is the villain of the Star Wars films

explanation.surface: A European screen baddie wears a short skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a garment, but it is the verb meaning to go around.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt a problem is to go round it, to evade it.

clue.text: Planet once placed outside large observatory's entrance

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one word goes round the single letter

parts.note: put means placed
L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of observatory

explanation.surface: A former planet sits outside the doorway of a big observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was counted the ninth planet until it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

clue.text: Famous dog originally dwelling around part of Switzerland?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the earlier word goes about the place name

parts.note: star used as an adjective, as in a star player
Bern is the Swiss capital and canton

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of dwelling

explanation.surface: A celebrated dog first lived near a Swiss region.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to the breed's origin: the St Bernard comes from the Alpine pass and hospice of that name in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Bernard is a large mountain-rescue dog breed, named after a Swiss Alpine hospice.

clue.text: Fish potentially with line you might catch?

indicators.note: to catch a word is to hear it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a row is a line, said the same as the fish eggs

explanation.surface: A fish that might be hooked on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' and 'line' suggest angling, but catch means hear. Fish eggs are 'fish potentially' because each could grow into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a fish, each of which could become a fish.

clue.text: Some musings on garage music session

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the words from musings into garage

explanation.surface: A few reflections on garage, the dance music genre.
explanation.walkthrough: Garage here is a style of electronic dance music, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A singsong is an informal session where a group sings together.

clue.text: Hand out gold shower component?

parts.note: to mete out is to hand out or allot
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Distributing gold fittings for a bathroom shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests the bathroom; it is a meteor shower, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor shower is made up of many individual meteors streaking across the sky.
